newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks better prices for Russian gas supplies.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks better prices for Russian gas supplies.

text.p: Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas said on Sunday it was not going to allow private gas firms to set prices for importing Russian natural gas to Bulgaria and would seek more favourable prices.

"Up to now we received Russian natural gas at the Bulgarian border (with Romania) at the price of $107.6 per 1,000 cubic metres, while gas prices in Europe and Turkey are lower by $10-$15," Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov told a news conference.
He said the Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company, Topenergy, in which Russia's Gazprom has 50 percent, has not agreed to lower prices of its gas supplies to Bulgaria.
Bulgargas, which holds a 25.1 percent share in Topenergy, may "revise its presence in the company if certain things are not changed", Filipov said.
Gazprom pays part of its credits from foreign firms by supplying them with natural gas volumes and Bulgargas plans to seal deals with such firms, he said.
"Gazprom creditors offer us favourable prices and we will swing towards such suppliers," Filipov said, adding that a 24-percent increase of gas prices for Bulgargas had not been realistic.
"We will not accept pressure from private companies," he said.

Petar Sabev, who is also a Bulgargas executive director, said his firm would seek credits from international lending institutions for the construction of a new underground natural gas storage facility.

Bulgargas needed more than $250 million credits for the construction of the new storage facility using abandoned salt caverns in the village of Mirovo near the industrial area of Devnya in northeastern Bulgaria.
Natural gas was found under the caverns.

"The Turkish state-owned Botas had offered credits for the construction of the Mirovo storage but we are forced to seek banking credits only as under the Bulgarian law the interest rate of a credit extended by a firm is not recognised as expenses," Sabev told the same news conference.
A gas storage facility would help Turkey when Russian gas supplies fall sharply in cold winters, officials said. For the last 10 years a gas pipeline has linked Bulgaria and Turkey.

Bulgargas, which has imported some six billion cubic metres of Russian natural gas last year to meet its domestic needs, reported a net profit of 960 million levs ($640,000) in 1996 against 879 million levs ($58,600) in 1995.

For the last 10 years Bulgaria has imported 3.34 billion cubic metres of Russian gas per year in return for its participation in construction work at Russia's Yambourg gas field under a 20-year intergovernmental agreement.
The first 10 years of the agreement during which Bulgaria has received gas without cash payment have expired last month.

A newly established Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company, named ZAO Inter Trans Investitsii i Torgovli, aimed at settling part of Bulgaria's payments of Russian gas supplies by barter, has already started work, Sabev said.
"The firm has sealed its first contracts for Bulgarian supplies of tins and cigarettes worth $20 million and we hope to ease our forthcoming payments of gas supplies to Russia," he said.
Sabev said there plans to explore four gas wells in Bulgaria as expectations were to discover more than 120 billion cubic metres of natural gas.
